audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim anti-Benjamin oath, Jabesh-gilead massacre, captive women, Shiloh abductions, tribal restoration, and closing refrain narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Mizpah marriage oath, lament over tribal loss, death oath against assembly absentees, targeting Jabesh-gilead, killing men, partnered women, and children, seizure of four hundred young women, peace offer to Rimmon survivors, insufficiency of captives, elders' legal evasion, Shiloh festival geography, vineyard ambush, abduction and forced marriage, family complaint management, Benjaminite rebuilding, and final no-king/right-in-own-eyes refrain.

verses.restored: Men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, No man from us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.

familiar.text: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpeh, saying, There shall not any of us give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife.

modern.text: Now the men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mizpah, saying, “Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite.”

original.text: וְאִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִשְׁבַּ֥ע בַּמִּצְפָּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לֹא יִתֵּ֥ן בִּתּ֛וֹ לְבִנְיָמִ֖ן לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: The people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before Divine. They lifted their voice and wept a great weeping.

familiar.text: And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;

modern.text: So the people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, lifting up their voices and weeping bitterly.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָעָם֙ בֵּֽית אֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֤שְׁבוּ שָׁם֙ עַד הָעֶ֔רֶב לִפְנֵ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ קוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּבְכּ֖וּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל

verses.restored: They said, Why, YHWH, Divine of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing today from Israel?

familiar.text: And said, O LORD God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?

modern.text: “Why, O LORD God of Israel,” they cried out, “has this happened in Israel? Today in Israel one tribe is missing!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לָמָ֗ה יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָ֥יְתָה זֹּ֖את בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהִפָּקֵ֥ד הַיּ֛וֹם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: On next day the people arose early, built there an altar, and offered ascending offerings and peace offerings.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people rose early, and built there an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

modern.text: The next day the people got up early, built an altar there, and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel said, Who is there from all tribes of Israel who did not come up in assembly to YHWH? For a great oath had been made concerning one who did not come up to YHWH at Mizpah, saying, Being put to death, he shall be put to death.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel said, Who is there among all the tribes of Israel that came not up with the congregation unto the LORD? For they had made a great oath concerning him that came not up to the LORD to Mizpeh, saying, He shall surely be put to death.

modern.text: The Israelites asked, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come to the assembly before the LORD?” For they had taken a solemn oath that anyone who failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah would surely be put to death.

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא עָלָ֧ה בַקָּהָ֛ל מִכָּל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה כִּי֩ הַשְּׁבוּעָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה הָיְתָ֗ה לַ֠אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָלָ֨ה אֶל יְהוָ֧ה הַמִּצְפָּ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: Children of Israel regretted concerning Benjamin their brother and said, One tribe has been cut off today from Israel.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, and said, There is one tribe cut off from Israel this day.

modern.text: And the Israelites grieved for their brothers, the Benjamites, and said, “Today a tribe is cut off from Israel.

original.text: וַיִּנָּֽחֲמוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל בִּנְיָמִ֖ן אָחִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נִגְדַּ֥ע הַיּ֛וֹם שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since we ourselves have sworn by YHWH not to give them from our daughters as wives?

familiar.text: How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the LORD that we will not give them of our daughters to wives?

modern.text: What should we do about wives for the survivors, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters in marriage?”

original.text: מַה נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים וַאֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְנוּ בַֽיהוָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י תֵּת לָהֶ֥ם מִבְּנוֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְנָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: They said, Who is one from tribes of Israel who did not come up to YHWH at Mizpah? Look, no man had come to camp from Jabesh-gilead to assembly.

familiar.text: And they said, What one is there of the tribes of Israel that came not up to Mizpeh to the LORD? And, behold, there came none to the camp from Jabeshgilead to the assembly.

modern.text: So they asked, “Which one of the tribes of Israel failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah?” And, in fact, no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִשִּׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא עָלָ֥ה אֶל יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹ֣א בָא אִ֧ישׁ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה מִיָּבֵ֥ישׁ גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶל הַקָּהָֽל

verses.restored: The people were counted, and look, there was no man there from inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.

familiar.text: For the people were numbered, and, behold, there were none of the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead there.

modern.text: For when the people were counted, none of the residents of Jabesh-gilead were there.

original.text: וַיִּתְפָּקֵ֖ד הָעָ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יָבֵ֥שׁ גִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: The congregation sent there twelve thousand men from sons of strength and commanded them, saying, Go and strike inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead by edge of sword, including women and little ones.

familiar.text: And the congregation sent thither twelve thousand men of the valiantest, and commanded them, saying, Go and smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the children.

modern.text: So the congregation sent 12,000 of their most valiant men and commanded them: “Go and put to the sword those living in Jabesh-gilead, including women and children.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ שָׁ֣ם הָעֵדָ֗ה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיְצַוּ֨וּ אוֹתָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר לְ֠כוּ וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם אֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יָבֵ֤שׁ גִּלְעָד֙ לְפִי חֶ֔רֶב וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף

verses.restored: This is the thing that you shall do: every male and every woman who has known lying with a male you shall devote to destruction.

familiar.text: And this is the thing that ye shall do, Ye shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman that hath lain by man.

modern.text: This is what you are to do: Devote to destruction every male, as well as every female who has had relations with a man.”

original.text: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ כָּל זָכָ֗ר וְכָל אִשָּׁ֛ה יֹדַ֥עַת מִשְׁכַּב זָכָ֖ר תַּחֲרִֽימוּ

verses.restored: They found among inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women who had not known a man by lying with a male. They brought them to camp at Shiloh, which is in land of Canaan.

familiar.text: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead four hundred young virgins, that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

modern.text: So they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women who had not had relations with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.

original.text: וַֽיִּמְצְא֞וּ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֗ד אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא יָדְעָ֛ה אִ֖ישׁ לְמִשְׁכַּ֣ב זָכָ֑ר וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אוֹתָ֤ם אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: All congregation sent and spoke to children of Benjamin who were at rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.

familiar.text: And the whole congregation sent some to speak to the children of Benjamin that were in the rock Rimmon, and to call peaceably unto them.

modern.text: Then the whole congregation sent a message of peace to the Benjamites who were at the rock of Rimmon.

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּסֶ֣לַע רִמּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from women of Jabesh-gilead, but they did not find enough for them.

familiar.text: And Benjamin came again at that time; and they gave them wives which they had saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead: and yet so they sufficed them not.

modern.text: And at that time the Benjamites returned and were given the women who were spared from Jabesh-gilead. But there were not enough women for all of them.

original.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב בִּנְיָמִן֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִיּ֔וּ מִנְּשֵׁ֖י יָבֵ֣שׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וְלֹֽא מָצְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן

verses.restored: The people regretted concerning Benjamin, because YHWH had made a breach among tribes of Israel.

familiar.text: And the people repented them for Benjamin, because that the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

modern.text: The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a void in the tribes of Israel.

original.text: וְהָעָ֥ם נִחָ֖ם לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּֽי עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Elders of congregation said, What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since women have been destroyed from Benjamin?

familiar.text: Then the elders of the congregation said, How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing the women are destroyed out of Benjamin?

modern.text: Then the elders of the congregation said, “What should we do about wives for those who remain, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְר֨וּ זִקְנֵ֣י הָעֵדָ֔ה מַה נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּֽי נִשְׁמְדָ֥ה מִבִּנְיָמִ֖ן אִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: They said, There must be an inheritance for survivors of Benjamin, so a tribe may not be wiped out from Israel.

familiar.text: And they said, There must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.

modern.text: They added, “There must be heirs for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְרֻשַּׁ֥ת פְּלֵיטָ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן וְלֹֽא יִמָּחֶ֥ה שֵׁ֖בֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: But we are not able to give them wives from our daughters, because children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed is one who gives a wife to Benjamin.

familiar.text: Howbeit we may not give them wives of our daughters: for the children of Israel have sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin.

modern.text: But we cannot give them our daughters as wives.” For the Israelites had sworn, “Cursed is he who gives a wife to a Benjamite.”

original.text: וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל לָתֵת לָהֶ֥ם נָשִׁ֖ים מִבְּנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי נִשְׁבְּע֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָר֕וּר נֹתֵ֥ן אִשָּׁ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִֽן

verses.restored: They said, Look, there is a feast of YHWH from days to days at Shiloh, which is north of Bethel, east of highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.

familiar.text: Then they said, Behold, there is a feast of the LORD in Shiloh yearly in a place which is on the north side of Bethel, on the east side of the highway that goeth up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.

modern.text: “But look,” they said, “there is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh, which is north of Bethel east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ הִנֵּה֩ חַג יְהוָ֨ה בְּשִׁל֜וֹ מִיָּמִ֣ים יָמִ֗ימָה אֲשֶׁ֞ר מִצְּפ֤וֹנָה לְבֵֽית אֵל֙ מִזְרְחָ֣ה הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ לִמְסִלָּ֔ה הָעֹלָ֥ה מִבֵּֽית אֵ֖ל שְׁכֶ֑מָה וּמִנֶּ֖גֶב לִלְבוֹנָֽה

verses.restored: They commanded children of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in wait in vineyards.

familiar.text: Therefore they commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in wait in the vineyards;

modern.text: So they commanded the Benjamites: “Go, hide in the vineyards

original.text: ויצו אֶת בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכ֖וּ וַאֲרַבְתֶּ֥ם בַּכְּרָמִֽים

verses.restored: Watch, and look: if daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances, then come out from vineyards and seize for yourselves, each man his wife, from daughters of Shiloh, and go to land of Benjamin.

familiar.text: And see, and, behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances, then come ye out of the vineyards, and catch you every man his wife of the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

modern.text: and watch. When you see the daughters of Shiloh come out to perform their dances, each of you is to come out of the vineyards, catch for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

original.text: וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם וְ֠הִנֵּה אִם יֵ֨צְא֥וּ בְנוֹת שִׁילוֹ֮ לָח֣וּל בַּמְּחֹלוֹת֒ וִֽיצָאתֶם֙ מִן הַכְּרָמִ֔ים וַחֲטַפְתֶּ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מִבְּנ֣וֹת שִׁיל֑וֹ וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֖ם אֶ֥רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן

verses.restored: When their fathers or their brothers come to contend with us, we will say to them, Show them favor for our sake, because we did not take for each man his wife in battle, nor did you give them to them at this time so as to become guilty.

familiar.text: And it shall be, when their fathers or their brethren come unto us to complain, that we will say unto them, Be favourable unto them for our sakes: because we reserved not to each man his wife in the war: for ye did not give unto them at this time, that ye should be guilty.

modern.text: When their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will tell them, ‘Do us a favor by helping them, since we did not get wives for each of them in the war. Since you did not actually give them your daughters, you have no guilt.’”

original.text: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּֽי יָבֹ֣אוּ אֲבוֹתָם֩ א֨וֹ אֲחֵיהֶ֜ם לרוב אֵלֵ֗ינוּ וְאָמַ֤רְנוּ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ חָנּ֣וּנוּ אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָקַ֛חְנוּ אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א אַתֶּ֛ם נְתַתֶּ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם כָּעֵ֥ת תֶּאְשָֽׁמוּ

verses.restored: Children of Benjamin did so. They carried away wives according to their number from dancing women whom they seized. They went and returned to their inheritance, built cities, and dwelt in them.

familiar.text: And the children of Benjamin did so, and took them wives, according to their number, of them that danced, whom they caught: and they went and returned unto their inheritance, and repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

modern.text: The Benjamites did as instructed and carried away the number of women they needed from the dancers they caught. They went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt their cities, and settled in them.

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ נָשִׁים֙ לְמִסְפָּרָ֔ם מִן הַמְּחֹלְל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֑לוּ וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ אֶל נַ֣חֲלָתָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: Children of Israel departed from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his clan; they went out from there, each man to his inheritance.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe and to his family, and they went out from thence every man to his inheritance.

modern.text: And at that time, each of the Israelites returned from there to his own tribe and clan, each to his own inheritance.

original.text: וַיִּתְהַלְּכ֨וּ מִשָּׁ֤ם בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אִ֥ישׁ לְשִׁבְט֖וֹ וּלְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וַיֵּצְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ

verses.restored: In those days there was no king in Israel; each one did what was right in one's own eyes.

familiar.text: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

original.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה

translation_notes: The oath not to give daughters to Benjamin is a human wartime vow. Like Jephthah's vow, it does not become righteous merely because YHWH's name is invoked. Harmful vows should be renounced, repaired, or lawfully released—not fulfilled through further victims.

Israel laments the possible loss of Benjamin but does not first lament Benjaminite civilians, Jabesh-gilead, the murdered concubine, or the women whose lives will be assigned as a solution. Grief for institutional continuity can obscure grief for persons.

A second oath threatens death to communities absent from Mizpah. The assembly uses one reckless oath to solve another, demonstrating how absolutist group promises multiply coercion rather than create faithfulness.
Jabesh-gilead's nonattendance does not justify massacre. Verse 10 explicitly includes women and little ones, making this collective punishment and mass killing of civilians.

The herem/devotion command in verse 11 is issued by the congregation in service of its plan. It must not be universalized as Divine permission for genocide, forced purity, or killing based on sex, relationship history, or community membership.

The four hundred young women are selected by male-defined sexual status after their families and community are killed. Their survival is captivity, not rescue; their lack of prior intercourse is not consent, availability, purity superiority, or a definition of womanhood.

Peace is proclaimed to the six hundred Benjaminite men while captive women are transferred to them. Reconciliation among armed men is purchased with women's autonomy and cannot be called restorative justice.
The elders treat women's bodies as a numerical resource for preserving male lineage. Tribal continuity does not override bodily autonomy, grief, kinship, or the right not to marry.
The Shiloh festival and dancing do not imply sexual or marital consent. Public celebration, clothing, movement, joy, youth, or presence outdoors never authorizes seizure.

The vineyard plan is organized abduction and forced marriage. The euphemism of 'take wives' must not conceal kidnapping, coercive confinement, likely sexual violence, and permanent disruption of the women's lives.
Verse 22 exploits a legal technicality: families did not voluntarily 'give' daughters, so the oath can be claimed intact. Technical compliance that engineers foreseeable abuse is not moral innocence.

Benjamin's rebuilding is narrated after women are seized, but restored cities do not repair murdered communities or coerced marriages. Survival of a tribe cannot be celebrated apart from the costs imposed on others.

The final refrain diagnoses a society where each acts according to private judgment. It does not prove that monarchy, authoritarianism, patriarchy, or a stronger coercive state would automatically create justice.
safety_note: Maximum anti-abduction, anti-forced-marriage, anti-genocide, and anti-women-as-property safeguards: Do not present Jabesh-gilead's massacre as obedience, the four hundred captives as saved brides, or the Shiloh abductions as romance. Oaths, tribal survival, lineage, festivals, family negotiations, and legal technicalities cannot override consent. Do not use sexual history to rank women, define gender, shame survivors, or mark anyone as available. The book ends with institutions preserving themselves by transferring violence onto women; that is the indictment, not the solution.
